caption:
Offer accepted in Georgetown. Now what?

1) Deposit: get it in by the deadline in your agreement. 2) Dates: put every condition date on your calendar. 3) Paperwork: send the signed agreement to your lender and your lawyer. 4) Inspection: book it early, while the condition period is open.

caption:
Buying near a Caledon creek? Check this first.

1) Ask: is the property near a creek, wetland or floodplain? 2) Why: regulated areas can affect permits for decks, pools and additions. 3) Who: your lawyer and realtor can help check, ideally before you make an offer.

Kitchener buyer? Ask for this first.

Ask for the last 12 months of utility bills. They show what the home really costs to heat, cool and power, which helps you plan your monthly budget. Your realtor can request them as part of your offer; the seller may decline, and costs vary with the household.

caption:
Mississauga condo? Ask for this first.

Ask your lawyer about the status certificate. 1) What it is: a condo corporation summary of fees, the reserve fund, special assessments and legal issues. 2) When to ask: right after your offer is accepted; ask your realtor about a review condition in your offer. 3) Who reviews it: your lawyer, so ask what to look for in the fee and reserve fund lines.

General information only, not legal advice.

Brampton new build? Find this page before you sign.

1) Find the Statement of Critical Dates, the first page of the addendum to your agreement. 2) Check the closing date and whether it is firm or tentative; tentative dates can be extended. 3) Know the outside closing date: if the home is not complete by then, you get a 30-day period to terminate. 4) Have your lawyer review the whole agreement before you sign.

Source: Tarion, coverage for closing dates and delays on new freehold homes (tarion.com), read Oct 29, 2026. Condos and other purchases follow different rules. General information only, not legal advice.

caption:
Waiting on rates? Do this math first.

1) Variable rate: your monthly mortgage could rise about $13 per $100,000 owed if your rate rises the full 0.25% (example 3.43% to 3.68%, 25-year amortization). 2) On a $500,000 mortgage that is about $66 more a month. 3) Fixed rate: no change until you renew; fixed rates follow bond yields.

Sources: Bank of Canada, Oct 28, 2026 (policy rate raised 0.25% to 2.5%); example rate: Ratehub, Oct 28, 2026. Calculated with Canadian semi-annual compounding. Examples only. Not financial or mortgage advice.

Pre-approved in Milton? Not approved yet.

1) Myth: pre-approved means approved. A pre-approval is an estimate of what a lender may lend you. 2) The lender still reviews the home itself and may order an appraisal. 3) A new car loan or a job change before closing can change your approval. 4) Ask your lender how long your rate hold lasts, and what could end it.
